operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case identifiers: tables 'wrestler'/'Elimination', columns 'Wrestler_ID','Days_held','Elimination_ID' — must double-quote with original spelling; case-insensitive lookup.
Tiny tables (wrestler=10 rows, Elimination=6) — no huge-table sampling needed; original_values fully read.
FK Elimination.Wrestler_ID (TEXT) -> wrestler.Wrestler_ID (INT): declared types differ across the FK edge; storage is text on child, integer on parent.
Elimination.Wrestler_ID samples include '7' which is NOT in wrestler PK samples 1-5 (parent has 10 rows, so 7 may exist; verify) — FK values are text-stored ints.
All columns declared TEXT except wrestler.Wrestler_ID INT; Days_held/Reign/Elimination_ID/Time are text-stored numbers/times, not typed.
No NOT NULL, no CHECK, no UNIQUE beyond PKs; all notnull=0 — TS will not enforce anything, insert failures only from PK dupes.
Time column is TEXT with 'HH:MM' format (no seconds) — dispatches to String fuzzer, not Time fuzzer.
Days_held is TEXT holding ints ('344','1') — String fuzzer, not Number; int-like string handling adds i±1.
Reign/Event/Team have distinct=2 — very low cardinality; TS String fuzzer will generate many fresh strings, breaking the 2-value domain.
Location values contain ' , ' (space-comma-space) and non-ASCII 'Villaño IV' in Name — charset a-zA-Z0-9() will not reproduce these.
Elimination_ID is TEXT PK with values '1'..'6' — String fuzzer generates random strings, PK uniqueness via sample_fresh_primary_keys.
No views/triggers/indexes beyond PKs; DDL is simple two-table schema.
operator_ts_expectations: wrestler.Wrestler_ID: Number fuzzer (INT, scale=0) -> ints in [-1,1] perturbed ±1/±2; will collide with PK often, rows dropped.
All TEXT columns: String fuzzer, length range from min/max element length (e.g. Name ~[3,15], Time ~[5,5]); fresh strings over a-zA-Z0-9() with 0.5 contaminate.
Reign/Event/Team (distinct=2): String fuzzer ignores the 2-value domain, generates random strings -> FN on queries filtering 'Live event'/'Wrestling World 1997'/'Team Orton'.
Days_held (int-like text): String fuzzer adds str(i±1) for int-like elements, so '344'->'345'/'343' plausible; but also random strings -> FN on numeric comparisons.
Time (TEXT 'HH:MM'): String fuzzer, not Time; will not produce valid HH:MM -> FN on time-range queries; contaminate may produce '00:11xyz'.
Elimination.Wrestler_ID FK: drawn from wrestler.Wrestler_ID final values (ints) but column is TEXT — sqlite stores as text, FK join works via affinity; TS does not enforce FK pragma.
Location ' , ' separator and non-ASCII Name: String fuzzer charset lacks comma/space patterns and non-ASCII -> FN on LIKE '%Japan%' style queries (Japan substring survives only if element reused).
Low cardinality (Reign=2, Event=2, Team=2): TS fresh-string bias causes FP on GROUP BY / DISTINCT queries (too many groups) and FN on equality filters.
PK collisions: Wrestler_ID Number fuzzer over [-1,1] with 10 rows -> many dupes dropped, effective table size shrinks; Elimination_ID String fuzzer random -> fewer collisions.
p=0.2 default, 0.3 chance whole-instance p=0 -> sometimes pure element reuse (good for low-cardinality), sometimes pure fresh (bad).
max_l0 cap (0.5 chance, rng*30) limits fresh draws -> after cap, reuses prior fresh values, partially mitigating low-cardinality FP.
No Date/Time/Bool fuzzers dispatched here; all String/Number — TS misses driven by String fuzzer's charset and fresh-vs-element balance.
